headline: US midterms deliver a shock for Republicans, the RBA hikes rates to an 18-year high, and Microsoft surges after blowout earnings — here's what matters for your Wednesday evening.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft surged last night after releasing its FY27 Q1 earnings, which smashed expectations. The market was reassured that its massive AI investment is paying off — Azure cloud growth was strong, and investors who had been nervous about spending too much on AI data centres breathed a sigh of relief. Best single-session performer in your portfolio.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up last night, buoyed by continued GTA 6 excitement. Pre-loading for the game has been moved up to November 10th and requires 212 GB of storage — a sign the launch is imminent. Analysts are increasingly tipping GTA 6 to be a record-breaking release, which is good for the long-term story here.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped today, weighed down by broader concern that a Democratic sweep in the US midterms could bring tougher AI regulation. When investors fear more rules on the AI industry, tech-focused ETFs like this one tend to sell off. Nothing has actually changed yet — it's a 'what if' reaction.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dipped again today as the lithium outlook remains under pressure. Citi has cut its lithium price forecasts, citing growing concerns about whether battery demand will grow fast enough to absorb the supply coming to market. This is a continuing headwind for the whole sector.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped slightly today in line with broad emerging market softness. The stronger US dollar and uncertainty around US foreign policy post-midterms tend to weigh on emerging market assets — no specific single catalyst today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased modestly today as the ASX 200 fell 0.59%. The RBA rate hike weighed on sentiment — higher rates can slow the economy and pressure company earnings. As a diversified global fund, the long-term story remains intact.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google was essentially flat last night, managing a tiny gain after a rough October in which shares fell around 17.5%. The market remains cautious about whether Google's search business can hold its ground as AI-powered competitors grow, but last night's session was quiet — no fresh negative news.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF edged down marginally today, moving in line with the slight dip in the ASX 200. No specific news. As a broadly diversified all-growth ETF, minor daily moves like this are completely normal noise — nothing to read into.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped very slightly on the ASX today, though it tracks the US market which was actually up last night (S&P 500 +0.36%, NASDAQ +0.83%). The minor difference is just timing — the ASX prices VTS based on the previous US close. The underlying US market was in positive territory.

watch_today.title: Microsoft earnings rocket — MSFT holding in great shape
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 2.74% last night after a stonking Q1 FY27 earnings report. Azure cloud and AI revenue came in strong, putting to rest fears that the company was overspending on AI infrastructure. For a long-term holder, this is exactly the kind of result that validates the investment thesis — sit tight and enjoy it.

watch_today.title: Citi slashes lithium price forecasts — PLS under sustained pressure
watch_today.detail: Citi has cut its lithium price forecasts, flagging that battery demand growth isn't keeping pace with the flood of new supply. Pilbara Minerals dropped again today and is now down over 61% from your cost base. The long-term lithium story (EVs, batteries) is still real, but it may take years to play out. If you believe in the thesis, hold — but this is a position worth reviewing if the investment case for a lithium recovery feels shaky to you.

watch_today.title: GXAI dips on AI regulation fears post-midterms
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF slipped 1.61% today as markets fretted that a Democratic sweep in the US midterms might bring stricter AI regulation. Nothing concrete has changed yet — no laws have passed. For a long-term holder in the AI theme, this kind of political noise is normal volatility. The dip could even be a topping-up opportunity if you're bullish on AI long term.

watch_today.title: RBA hikes to 18-year high — watch the impact on ASX and your ETFs
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank lifted the cash rate again this week to its highest level in 18 years, warning that inflation will be painful for at least another year. Higher rates slow the economy, squeeze household budgets, and can weigh on ASX-exposed holdings like VDHG and DHHF. The vote was split though, suggesting this may be near the peak — keep an eye on the next RBA meeting for signals of a pause.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 pre-loading moved to November 10 — TTWO launch imminent
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's GTA 6 is now pre-loading from November 10th and requires a massive 212 GB of storage. Analysts are calling it a potential record-breaking title. The share price has been recovering and the long-term bull case — massive game revenue over years — is very much alive. Hold and watch the launch reviews closely.

watch_today.title: Gold hits $4,032 — a tailwind for defensive portfolios
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 2.34% last night to over US$4,032 per ounce. It's being driven by geopolitical tension (US-Iran conflict, midterm uncertainty) and investors seeking safety. While you don't hold gold directly, it's a useful signal — when gold spikes like this, it usually means markets are nervous. Worth knowing as context for why risk assets like GXAI and VGE are soft.

world.summary: It's a big news day globally — the US midterm results are shaking up Washington, the US-Iran conflict is escalating and then potentially de-escalating in the same breath, and gold is spiking as investors seek safety.

stories.title: Republicans suffer stunning midterm defeat — Democrats sweep key races
stories.why_it_matters: In a result that surprised most pundits, Democrats performed strongly in the US midterm elections, with Republicans suffering what's being described as a 'stunning defeat.' This is significant because it limits Trump's ability to push his legislative agenda through Congress. Markets are reacting to what a divided or Democrat-leaning Congress means for tax policy, regulation, and spending — particularly around AI and tech sectors, which had been hoping for a lighter regulatory touch under Republican control.

stories.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island — but both sides are now talking about a deal
stories.why_it_matters: The US reportedly struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, escalating military tensions significantly. At the same time, Trump said in an interview that Iran 'wants a deal and it could happen,' and Bloomberg reports both sides are reviewing peace proposals. Iran's president also said returning to full-scale war benefits 'no one.' This push-pull between military action and diplomatic back-channel talks is keeping oil markets jumpy — crude is sitting above US$96 a barrel.

stories.title: Israel warns US and Gulf allies Iran is planning chemical weapons use
stories.why_it_matters: Israel has reportedly warned US and Gulf allies that Iran is planning to deploy chemical weapons. This is an extraordinary and alarming claim if true, and would dramatically raise the stakes in the Middle East conflict. No independent verification has emerged yet, but the report alone is enough to rattle energy markets and push investors toward safe havens like gold — which jumped over 2% last night to above US$4,000 an ounce.

stories.title: Trump says he will accept midterm election results — courts block election pressure
stories.why_it_matters: In an interview, Trump said he would accept the midterm election results — a notable statement given the controversy surrounding the 2020 election. Meanwhile, courts moved to rebuff Trump's attempts to pressure state election officials. These two developments together suggest the legal guardrails around US elections are holding, which markets generally view as a stabilising factor for US political risk.

stories.title: Global economic outlook for 2027 looking uncertain — HKU and Fudan forums warn of fragile markets
stories.why_it_matters: Leading economists at the University of Hong Kong and Fudan University forums are warning that global markets are fragile heading into 2027, with AI-related capital spending, geopolitical tension, and sticky inflation all creating risks. For everyday investors, this is a reminder that diversification across geographies and asset classes — exactly what holdings like VDHG and DHHF are designed to do — remains important when the outlook is uncertain.

politics.summary: The RBA has hiked interest rates again, hitting an 18-year high — and the split vote on the board suggests this could be near the peak. Households and mortgage holders are feeling the squeeze.

stories.title: RBA hikes to 18-year high — warns inflation pain has another year to run
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised the cash rate again this week, pushing it to its highest level in 18 years. The RBA warned that inflation will continue to bite for at least another year. The board vote was split, which is a signal that some members think this could be the last hike for a while — a 'pause' may be coming. For mortgage holders, this means higher repayments again. For savers, it means better returns on deposits.

stories.title: Big banks pass on the rate hike — mortgage holders hit immediately
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's major banks have already moved to pass the RBA's rate hike directly onto variable mortgage customers. For a typical borrower, this means hundreds of dollars more per year in repayments. The timing — described as a 'Friday the 13th horror' by some outlets — is tough for households already under cost-of-living pressure. The flipside is that savings accounts and term deposits are paying better rates than they have in years.

stories.title: AFR: 'Labor's economic model is broken and households are paying the bill'
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian Financial Review is running a sharp critique of the Albanese government's economic management, arguing that Labor's approach has contributed to persistent inflation that is forcing the RBA to keep hiking. The piece argues ordinary households are bearing the cost. This is a political pressure point — with the next federal election on the horizon, cost-of-living and interest rates are shaping up as key battleground issues.

ai.summary: The AI world is buzzing after Google unveiled a powerful new Gemini model, while the US midterm results are stoking fears about stricter AI regulation — sending some tech stocks lower.

stories.title: Google reveals Gemini 4 Carbon — claims it's the least likely AI model to hallucinate
stories.why_it_matters: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model, narrowly beating Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 on key benchmarks. Most notably, Google claims it's the least likely of any major AI model to 'hallucinate' — that's when an AI confidently states something that's just plain wrong. Reducing hallucinations is one of the biggest practical hurdles to deploying AI in business and professional settings, so this is a meaningful step forward. Good news for GOOG holders — it shows Google is staying competitive in the AI race.

stories.title: AI regulation fears spike after Democrat midterm gains — tech stocks feel the heat
stories.why_it_matters: Markets are pricing in the risk that stronger Democrat results in the US midterms could lead to more aggressive AI regulation. Europe's markets opened lower on this concern, and Japan's AI-focused stocks fell for a fourth straight session. For Australian holders of AI-exposed ETFs like GXAI, this is a short-term headwind — but actual regulation takes years to become law, so the long-term AI growth story hasn't changed.

stories.title: The great AI rift: Meta and Palantir vs OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google
stories.why_it_matters: A fascinating split is opening up in the AI industry. On one side: Meta and Palantir, who favour open-source AI — that means publishing the code freely so anyone can use and modify it. On the other: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, who keep their most powerful models closed and commercial. This isn't just a technical debate — it's about who controls AI, who profits from it, and what regulations look like. For investors, it matters because it shapes which companies dominate the AI economy in coming years.

stories.title: US tech stocks recover after AI spending selloff
stories.why_it_matters: After a rough patch where investors panicked about how much money big tech companies were pouring into AI infrastructure, US tech stocks staged a recovery last night. Microsoft's strong earnings (showing AI investment IS generating revenue) helped reassure markets that the spending isn't just burning cash. This is a broader positive signal for AI-exposed holdings in your portfolio like GXAI and MSFT.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was broadly positive — the NASDAQ led gains as Microsoft's earnings impressed. The ASX pulled back today as the RBA rate hike weighed on sentiment. Gold is surging on Middle East tension, and oil is nudging higher.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: The ASX fell today, dragged down by the RBA rate hike and global uncertainty around the US midterms. Rate-sensitive sectors like property and consumer stocks were hit hardest.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: The S&P 500 edged higher last night, supported by Microsoft's strong earnings report and a mild recovery in tech stocks after recent AI-spending jitters.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ outperformed last night, with Microsoft's 2.74% jump and broader tech recovery leading the charge. AI regulation fears are emerging but haven't dominated yet.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold had a big night, jumping over 2% to above US$4,000 an ounce. Middle East tensions — including the US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and the chemical weapons warning — are driving investors into safe haven assets.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil ticked slightly higher as Middle East tensions remain elevated. With the US-Iran situation volatile, any escalation could push prices significantly higher — worth watching.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar is essentially flat, sitting just below 70 US cents. The RBA hike provided some support but global uncertainty is keeping a lid on gains.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done and dusted — the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in a thriller at Accor Stadium. The footy world is now turning to off-season moves and rugby crossovers.

stories.title: Roosters beat Knights 19-18 in NRL Grand Final classic
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters won the 2026 NRL Grand Final, defeating the Knights 19-18 in a one-point nail-biter at Accor Stadium. It was the kind of finish that Grand Finals are made for — a one-point margin with everything on the line. Roosters fans are celebrating a premiership, while the Knights will be left wondering what might have been.

stories.title: Angus Crichton makes NRL-to-rugby switch — Cheika's Waratahs recruit
stories.why_it_matters: NRL forward Angus Crichton is heading to rugby union, signing with the Waratahs under coach Michael Cheika. It's one of the most high-profile NRL-to-rugby crossovers in recent memory. Cheika reportedly reached out personally after Crichton's NRL triumph, and the move marks a new chapter for both player and club.

stories.title: Bulldogs dismiss Adam Walker rumours as Moses Burton's future stays unclear
stories.why_it_matters: The Canterbury Bulldogs have officially denied rumours linking them to a move for Adam Walker, though Moses Burton's contract situation at the club remains unresolved. With the off-season transfer window heating up, the Bulldogs' roster planning is under the spotlight. Burton was a key contributor this season and his future will be watched closely by rival clubs.

stories.title: BYD replaces Nissan as Hawthorn Hawks AFL sponsor
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD has signed on as the Hawthorn Hawks' major AFL and AFLW sponsor, replacing Nissan. It's a sign of BYD's aggressive push into Australian brand awareness — and of Japanese carmaker Nissan's continuing retreat from sponsorship commitments as it faces its own financial pressures globally. For AFL fans it's a curiosity; for anyone watching the EV sector, it's another reminder of BYD's expanding footprint in Australia.

stories.title: Djokovic feeling better, playing better — sees light at end of tunnel
stories.why_it_matters: Novak Djokovic says he's feeling better physically and his game is coming together again, with the tennis great describing a positive turn in his form and health. After a difficult stretch with injury concerns, Djokovic's return to form is big news heading into the end-of-year tour. At 39, every competitive campaign could be his last — making each tournament he enters appointment viewing.
